serp_features.ai_overview: Present in all three cities and identical. Leads with an average of $38,252 (NSW $42,322), a 10-item category list (venue about $17,518, photography about $3,657, and so on) and state averages. These are the 2026 industry survey figures widely attributed to Easy Weddings (a blocked competitor). Cited sources: managingmatrimony.com.au, paperlust.co, bridebook.com, vowsandveils.com.au, Reddit r/AusFinance and an SMH article. Closes with 'couples spend about 23% more than budget' and Reddit consensus that many weddings cost far less.

cross_market_insights: All three cities show the same AI Overview, anchored on the 2026 industry survey average of $38,252 (attributed to Easy Weddings, blocked). Organic results mostly repeat that figure or older ones ($36,000, $36,200, $27,228, $44,000, $65,482).

Figures and sources used by the top 3: industry surveys (Easy Weddings via pix.wedding and TikTok), unsourced vendor numbers (Pillingers, Ultima, Peta), and second-hand 'ASIC Moneysmart' citations (smfp.au; Swoosh at #4 Melbourne cites Moneysmart $36,200). Our own hub notes Australia's government figure comes from a 2013 survey. Nobody links ABS or explains that ABS collects marriage counts, not costs.

GAP 1: no ranking page says plainly that there is no current official Australian average, or explains why survey averages mislead (self-selected samples, mean vs median, what is included, sponsor bias).
GAP 2: no page addresses the luxury tier (AUD 150K+) or how costs scale by category above the 'average'.
GAP 3: no page compares a home wedding with a destination wedding for Australians.
GAP 4: costs couples forget (wet weather plan, supplier meals, surcharges, deposits and cancellation rights under Australian Consumer Law) are barely covered; nobody cites the ACCC.
Our 2020 page ranks #2 in Sydney and Brisbane, so the 301 into the kept URL should carry real equity. The kept URL itself is not in the top 10 of any city.

Freshness is weak across the SERP (2014, 2015, 2017, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2024 dates on page 1), so a current, well-sourced explainer has a realistic opening even without a headline figure. Risk: the AI Overview rewards a single number, so our featured-snippet chance is lower; we compete on trust and depth instead.
payload.recommended_angle: The honest Australian guide: why no current official average exists (ABS, Moneysmart), why the survey averages mislead, what actually drives cost category by category at the luxury end, the costs people forget (ACCC on deposits and contracts), and how a destination wedding compares, with a Wedded Advisor handling the invisible work.
